title: Kasol to Jispa
summary: A car trip from Jaipur to the Parvati valley and on into Lahaul: Kasol, Manikaran, Manali, Sissu and Jispa, with snow on the road up to Shinku La. 17 to 20 May 2026.
story:
A car trip from Jaipur into the Himalaya, in May 2026: the Parvati valley around Kasol and Manikaran, then Manali, the Atal Tunnel and Lahaul for Sissu and Jispa, and up the road towards the Shinku La pass until it started to snow. These are the photographs, the route and the details worth knowing.

## The route

Four days, 17 to 20 May 2026, by the dates in the photographs. The first two were in the Parvati valley: a camp about 3 km west of Kasol village, and Manikaran, 3.5 km further up the valley. By the evening of the 18th the photographs are on the Manali side, at Koshla and in Solang Valley. Then came the long day north on the 19th: Manali to Sissu is 41 km through the Atal Tunnel, Sissu to Jispa is another 52 km, and the afternoon went on up the Shinku La road until the snow. Jispa was where the night of the 19th was spent, and the last morning went back down to Sissu.

The climb is steady. The camp is at about 1,470 m by the photographs' GPS, Kasol village at about 1,580 m, Sissu at about 3,120 m and Jispa at about 3,200 m. On the last stretch the phone logged about 4,030 m, 4,190 m and, with snow falling, 4,877 m, roughly 2 km short of Shinku La (5,091 m).

## Getting there from Jaipur

By road Jaipur to Kasol is roughly 780 to 800 km, which is about 15 to 17 hours of driving with halts. That figure is an estimate: Jaipur to Manali is listed at about 800 to 820 km, and the Kasol road leaves the Manali highway at Bhuntar.

The usual way is NH-48 from Jaipur to Delhi, NH-44 on to Chandigarh (three to four hours from Delhi), then the hill road through Kiratpur Sahib, Bilaspur, Mandi and the Aut Tunnel to Bhuntar. From Bhuntar the Kasol road runs about 30 km up the Parvati valley. It is narrow, so it is worth driving in daylight.

## Over to Lahaul

From Kasol the way north is back down to Bhuntar, through Kullu and on to Manali (about 75 km, two and a half to three hours). Then comes the Atal Tunnel, 9.02 km long and opened in 2020. It replaced the climb over the Rohtang Pass and drops you into Lahaul, with Sissu just beyond the north portal. From Manali, Keylong is 71 km, Jispa 93 km and Darcha 99 km.

## The Shinku La road

At Darcha the road to the Shinku La pass leaves the Manali–Leh highway (it starts at Barsi Bridge, near Darcha Sumdol). The pass, at 5,091 m by Wikipedia (other sources say 4,900 to 5,100 m), is on the border between Lahaul and Zanskar, and the road over it leads to Padum. It is not an all-weather road: the pass is usually snowbound from October to April and prone to avalanches, and a 4.1 km tunnel under it has been under construction since July 2024. The photographs show the road at about 4,030 m, 4,190 m and, with snow falling, 4,877 m.

## Good to know

The Manali–Leh highway usually opens for the season in the first weeks of May and stays open until October. At this height the weather can close a road at any time, so check the BRO or Lahaul and Spiti road status before heading up. Jispa is cold even in summer, with nights of 3 to 5 °C. Above 4,000 m, go slowly and drink plenty of water.

The way back is the same road in reverse: Sissu to Manali is 41 km, then Jaipur is another 800 to 820 km.

stops.note: Roughly 780 to 800 km by road, about 15 to 17 hours with halts: NH-48 to Delhi, NH-44 to Chandigarh, then Kiratpur Sahib, Bilaspur, Mandi and the Aut Tunnel to Bhuntar.
stops.tip: From Bhuntar the Kasol road is about 30 km and narrow. Drive it in daylight.

stops.note: The first photographs of the trip, in the valley before Kasol. The phone put them near Bhuntar, about 15 km short of the village, with a margin of about 1.4 km.

stops.place: The camp by the river, near Kasol
stops.note: About 3 km west of Kasol village and about 1,470 m up, by the photographs' GPS. Kasol itself sits on the Parvati at about 1,580 m, 30 km from Bhuntar and 3.5 km from Manikaran. Boulders in the river, a small cairn, and a pine forest for the last light.

days.title: Monday 18 May: Manikaran, then on to Manali

stops.note: 3.5 km up the valley from Kasol, about 15 minutes. A pilgrimage town for Hindus and Sikhs: the Manikaran Sahib gurdwara and a Shiva temple sit side by side, with hot springs at 64 to 80 °C.
stops.tip: Cover your head and take off your shoes at the gurdwara and the temples. Keep clear of the hot water.

stops.note: By the evening the photographs are on the Manali side: this one is at Koshla, just north of the town, about 75 km from Kasol by road. A roadside stop at dusk was in Solang Valley, about 9 km further north (that photo has no time, so it is placed by its position in the camera's numbering).

days.title: Tuesday 19 May: Over the Atal Tunnel to Lahaul

stops.note: The Atal Tunnel runs 9.02 km under the Pir Panjal range and opened in 2020, so the Rohtang Pass is no longer in the way.
stops.tip: Check the road status for Lahaul and Spiti before leaving Manali. Snow and landslides can close the road beyond Keylong.

stops.place: North of the Atal Tunnel, near Sissu
stops.note: Out of the tunnel at about 3,120 m, with Sissu village about 7 km to the north-west. Sissu is 41 km from Manali, on the Chandra river.
52 km on from Sissu, at about 3,200 m on the Bhaga river. 22 km north of Keylong and 7 km south of Darcha.

stops.place: On the road up to Shinku La
stops.note: Past Darcha the road leaves the Manali–Leh highway and climbs the side valley towards the Shinku La pass, which leads over to Zanskar. The mountains turn white. The phone logged about 4,030 m here.

stops.place: Snow on the Shinku La road
stops.note: Snow was falling at about 4,877 m, roughly 2 km short of the pass (5,091 m).
stops.tip: At this height, go slowly and drink plenty of water. Altitude sickness is real.

stops.note: On the way back down from the Shinku La road, a few km north of Jispa, with the last sun on the peaks.
Back in Jispa for the night, with the blue hour over the rooftops. Nights here are cold even in summer.
About 50 m high, across the Chandra river from the village, and fed by the snow above it. Sissu is 41 km from Manali, and from there Jaipur is another 800 to 820 km by road.

title: Ujjain and Omkareshwar
summary: A family trip over the Republic Day long weekend, 25 to 27 January 2026: Ram Ghat, Mahakaleshwar, the Siddhavat banyan and Kaal Bhairav in Ujjain, the Narmada, Omkareshwar and Mahakal Lok.
story:
A family trip to Ujjain and Omkareshwar in Madhya Pradesh over the Republic Day long weekend, 25 to 27 January 2026. I went with my parents, my bhua (my father's sister) and a friend of my father's with his family. We went to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, the Kaal Bhairav temple and the Siddhavat banyan in Ujjain, then to Omkareshwar on the Narmada, and finished back in Ujjain at Mahakal Lok. These are the photographs, the videos and what I found out about each place.

## The route

Three days, 25 to 27 January 2026. The first was all Ujjain: Ram Ghat on the Shipra in the morning, the Mahakaleshwar temple around noon, then the Siddhavat banyan and the Kaal Bhairav temple after dark. On the Monday, which was Republic Day, we went to Omkareshwar, about 140 km south by road (sources say 135 to 150 km). We stopped at the Narmada at Barwaha on the way, reached Omkareshwar in the afternoon and stayed until the evening lights were on. On the Tuesday we were back in Ujjain, in Mahakal Lok, by about noon.

## The long weekend

Republic Day fell on a Monday in 2026, so it was a long weekend, and the crowds showed it. At 10:23 on the Sunday morning the road towards Ram Ghat was one slow stream of people. The line at Mahakaleshwar took about 45 minutes: the photograph of the rose is from 11:40 and the one inside the hall is from 12:24. At Kaal Bhairav the line climbed the steps to the gate in the dark. At Omkareshwar the crowd was so heavy that all of us had to sit inside one single auto.

## Mahakaleshwar and Mahakal Lok

Mahakaleshwar is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and the only one that faces south. The lingam is said to be self-manifested, svayambhu, and the temple stands near the Shipra river and the Rudrasagar lake. Mahakal Lok is the pedestrian corridor of about 900 m that leads from a visitor plaza to the temple. It opened on 11 October 2022 and is lined with sandstone pillars, murals and statues telling the stories of Shiva. Reports disagree about how many statues there are (figures from 76 to 200 appear), so I have not counted them.

## Siddhavat

The Siddhavat is a sacred banyan on the bank of the Shipra at Bhairavgarh. It is believed that Mata Parvati planted it for Bar Amavasya pooja, and it is still there. Other stories are told about it too: one says Lord Ram performed the last rites for his father Dasharatha under it, and another says a ruler once had it cut down and covered the stump with iron plates, after which it grew back. At night the trees are lit green.

## Kaal Bhairav

The Kaal Bhairav temple is regarded as the guardian temple of Ujjain, and Kaal Bhairav as the city's kotwal. Alcohol is offered to the deity here. It is one of five tantric offerings, and today it is the only one actually made. Temple tradition puts the age of the temple at around 6,000 years; the original temple is believed to have been built by a king named Bhadrasen, and it is mentioned in the Skanda Purana.

## Omkareshwar

Omkareshwar is on Mandhata island in the Narmada. The island is said to be shaped like the sign Om when seen from above, which is a tradition and not a surveyed fact. There is a Jyotirlinga temple here, and Mamleshwar is across the river (sources disagree on which bank each is on, so I have not said). Boats run along the ghat, and a suspension bridge crosses the river.

## Good to know

The Simhastha Kumbh is held on the Shipra at Ujjain every twelve years, with Ram Ghat as the main bathing ghat, and the next one is in 2028. The aarti times and the length of the lines change from day to day, so check locally. On a holiday weekend expect long lines and slow roads, and plan the day around them.

stops.note: The main bathing ghat on the Shipra, where the Simhastha Kumbh bathing is held every twelve years (the next is in 2028). The road towards it was packed on the long weekend.
One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, and the only one that faces south. We were in the line from about 11:40 and inside the hall by 12:24.
stops.tip: Expect a long line on weekends and holidays. We waited about 45 minutes.

stops.note: The sacred banyan on the bank of the Shipra at Bhairavgarh. It is believed that Mata Parvati planted it for Bar Amavasya pooja. The trees are lit green at night.
The guardian temple of Ujjain. The line climbs the steps to the gate, and the offering here is alcohol.
About 140 km south from Ujjain by road (sources say 135 to 150 km). It was Republic Day, and the roads were busy.
A stop at the river, about 11 km from Omkareshwar in a straight line. I went into the water, and the video is among the postcards.
Omkareshwar is on Mandhata island in the Narmada, said to be shaped like the sign Om. We got there through a heavy crowd, all of us in one auto.
The bridges, the ghats and the crowd, all lit up and reflected in the Narmada.
The corridor of about 900 m from the visitor plaza to the temple, opened on 11 October 2022, with statues and murals of the stories of Shiva.
